doc.headline: Atlas-M costs {cost.gap.atlas-m.atlas-l.multiple} what Atlas-L does at this run's unnamed routing, with no behaviour check separating them; Atlas-L's extra overall quality is the owner's to price.
doc.lede: The cheaper models save more but confirm before account changes less often than Atlas-M, and Brisk-S resolves fewer troubleshooting issues. With no price set for a point of overall quality, Atlas-M is the better buy below {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} per point per 1,000 conversations, Atlas-L above {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}.
doc.flag: No control, gate or price per point was declared: this run prices the trade, and the concierge owner makes the call.

caveats.material_if: It decides the pick itself, which waits on a price per point of overall quality or floors on the behaviour checks; it does not touch the measured gaps the trade is built from.

Only if scoring the arms paired on their shared cases would separate a behaviour-check gap the unpaired intervals leave open, such as Atlas-L's tool-call lead over Atlas-M (from {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.toolcall.task.research.interval}). Pairing narrows intervals, so it could add a reason to pay for Atlas-L but would not undo a gap already clear of zero.

Only if the unnamed judge of the behaviour checks is harsher on the smaller models' style, which would shrink their shortfalls and make Brisk-S a stronger low-price option. The overall-quality judge is calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings at {judged.overall.agreement} agreement, so the price per point does not rest on the unnamed one.

Only if Atlas-L's lead in overall quality is partly the luck of the best of several: a fresh run would tend to read it lower, which would cheapen the case for Atlas-L, not Atlas-M. Its unpaired interval, from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}, sits clear of zero.

caveats.label: Cost routing and coverage unknown
caveats.material_if: Only if another provider serving one of these models, or trials that reported no cost, would reorder the costs: the snapshot names no provider or pricing for any model and does not say how many trials reported a cost, so every price holds for this run's routing only. Open-70B, an open-weights model, is the most exposed, since its price depends on who hosts it.

decision.text: Moving from Atlas-M to Atlas-L costs {cost.gap.atlas-l.atlas-m.per_1k|abs} more per 1,000 conversations and buys {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain|abs} points of overall quality (from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}); on the behaviour checks the two are not told apart. Brisk-S costs {cost.gap.brisk-s.atlas-m.multiple} what Atlas-M does but trails it clearly on troubleshooting.

A point of overall quality worth less than {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} per 1,000 conversations favours Atlas-M, more than {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} favours Atlas-L; between the two this run does not settle it. On overall quality alone Brisk-S is the better buy below {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} a point. On point estimates Open-70B is never the better buy; inside the band from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} this run does not separate it from Brisk-S and Atlas-M.

Ours, not a recommendation: Atlas-M, which the price frontier favours from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} a point; no behaviour check separates it from Atlas-L, and its tail latency is shorter in every task. Below that band we would still pass over Brisk-S: in troubleshooting it resolves the issue {task.trouble.brisk-s.resolves.mean} of the time against {task.trouble.atlas-m.resolves.mean}, and confirms before account changes {task.trouble.brisk-s.confirms.mean} against {task.trouble.atlas-m.confirms.mean}.
The concierge owner declares a price per point of overall quality, or floors on the behaviour checks that matter (confirming before account changes above all).
Every cost is this run's provider routing, which the snapshot does not name; another host for any of these models, Open-70B above all, could move the price bands.

claims.text: On this run's unnamed provider routing, each step up in overall quality costs more per point: Brisk-S to Atlas-M from {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.brisk-s.atlas-m.overall.per_point_high_unpaired} per point per 1,000 conversations, Atlas-M to Atlas-L from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired} to {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_high_unpaired}.

claims.text: Atlas-L leads Atlas-M on overall quality in every task that carries traffic, most in troubleshooting at {compare.atlas-l.atlas-m.overall.task.trouble.difference} points; on speculation bait, the test slice, the two are not told apart.

evidence.caption: Task rows only, no overall row: the gap pooled by traffic share is {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain} (from {price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.gain_interval_unpaired}).

claims.text: In troubleshooting Atlas-M is not told apart from Atlas-L on any check, while Brisk-S resolves the issue {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.resolves.task.trouble.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M.

evidence.caption: Troubleshooting pass rates on the behaviour checks read there, with their intervals.

claims.text: Both cheaper models confirm before account changes less often than Atlas-M: Open-70B by {compare.atlas-m.open-70b.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} points (from {compare.atlas-m.open-70b.confirms.task.trouble.interval}), Brisk-S by {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.confirms.task.trouble.difference|abs} (from {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.confirms.task.trouble.interval}).

evidence.caption: Atlas-M less Open-70B on confirming before account changes in troubleshooting, with its unpaired interval.
Atlas-M less Brisk-S on confirming before account changes in troubleshooting, with its unpaired interval.

claims.text: On research questions Atlas-M and Atlas-L are not told apart on tool use, citing or unsupported claims; Brisk-S and Open-70B score lower on all three, though Brisk-S's citing gap to Atlas-M is not separated from zero (from {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.cites.task.research.interval}).

evidence.caption: Research-question pass rates on the behaviour checks read there, with their intervals.

claims.text: When baited, Brisk-S declines to speculate {compare.atlas-m.brisk-s.declines.task.specul.difference|abs} points less often than Atlas-M; speculation bait carries {task.specul.share} of traffic, so this is a test of behaviour, not a rate users will meet.

evidence.caption: Declines to speculate on speculation bait, each model with its interval.

claims.text: In persona small talk Open-70B is not told apart from Atlas-M on overall quality, {task.persona.open-70b.overall.mean} against {task.persona.atlas-m.overall.mean} (gap from {compare.open-70b.atlas-m.overall.task.persona.interval}), nor from either Atlas model on staying in character, at {task.persona.open-70b.cost_per_1k.mean} per 1,000 conversations against {task.persona.atlas-m.cost_per_1k.mean} on this run's unnamed provider routing.

evidence.caption: Persona small talk: overall quality, cost per 1,000 conversations and staying in character for each model.

claims.text: Atlas-L is the slowest model in every task; on research questions its tail latency reaches {task.research.atlas-l.latency_s.p95} against {task.research.atlas-m.latency_s.p95} for Atlas-M, and no model dropped a trial to get there.

evidence.caption: Latency from median to tail for each model in every task.

Inside each interval band between those, this run does not settle the pick; in the lower band it does not separate Open-70B from Brisk-S and Atlas-M either, though on point estimates Open-70B is never the better buy. Brisk-S's behaviour-check shortfalls are not priced in.

method.text: {scoreboard.atlas-l.cases} conversations per model over the tasks listed under traffic shares, the same count for each; repeats are not stated. No trial was lost or failed for any model.

A judged score per conversation; the judge is calibrated on {judged.overall.calibration_ratings} human ratings with {judged.overall.agreement} agreement. Overall figures pool the tasks by traffic share.
Pass-or-fail judged checks, each read only in the task it applies to. The campaign does not define what passing each means beyond its name, nor who judges them.

Billing {task.billing.share}, persona small talk {task.persona.share}, troubleshooting {task.trouble.share}, research questions {task.research.share}, speculation bait {task.specul.share}: speculation bait is a test slice and counts toward no overall figure.

At the level each block prints, uncorrected. With no control and no paired contrasts, every gap between two models combines each model's own interval as if they ran different cases, which reads wider than a paired interval would. Price bands are read on these unpaired intervals throughout.
Cost per 1,000 conversations, weighted by traffic share. The provider serving each model and how many trials reported a cost are not stated, and no monthly volume was declared.
Median and tail percentile per task, in seconds.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and price-frontier claim answer the reader's questions. Nothing was declared, so the owner prices the trade. Atlas-M is a third of Atlas-L's cost ($31.37 against $75.05), and no behaviour check tells them apart. A point of overall quality has to be worth more than $22.05 before Atlas-L is the better buy, and below $11.09 Atlas-M is. The main risks are both on the first screen: the cheaper models fall short on the behaviour checks, and the provider routing is unknown (in Watch). I recomputed the price bands with price_tradeoff and they match: a gain of 2.96 (+1.981 to +3.939) for $44, so $14.76 a point ($11.09 to $22.05).

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: Each claim matches its block row by row. troubleshooting-checks: Brisk-S resolves the issue 90 - 74 = 16 points less often than Atlas-M. confirms-gap: 98 - 81 = 17 (+11 to +23). speculation-test: 98 - 81 = 17. persona: 97 against 95, inside overlapping intervals. atlas-gap-by-task: all four traffic-bearing tasks clear zero, and speculation bait does not (-1.5 to +3.5). latency: Atlas-L has the highest p95 in every task in the appendix. No row contradicts its sentence or the headline.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Atlas-M's weak axis, 2.96 points of overall quality, is up front. Two statements go further than their intervals. First, the decision block says 'Open-70B is the better buy at no price', and the price-frontier caption says it is 'never the cheapest way to a point'. That holds only on point estimates. Its pooled quality (85.49, ±0.69) is just 0.79 above Brisk-S's (about -0.2 to +1.8 unpaired). Near the top of its interval it would be the best buy from about $3.7 to $5.4 a point, which overlaps the $4.15 to $6.11 band the page already calls unsettled. Second, research-checks says Brisk-S 'scores lower on all three' as if separated, but its citing gap to Atlas-M is +5 with an interval of 0 to +10.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: Nothing left out would change the decision. Cost by task and latency by task keep the same order, and both are in the appendix. options_dominance confirms the code withheld a dominance call because cost is the only declared axis, so dropping it is right. Per-task quality for Open-70B is in the appendix, including persona small talk, where it scores 90 against Atlas-M's 88. One correction: the reason given ('both sit below Atlas-M in most tasks') hides that Open-70B is level with or above Atlas-M on persona small talk. The routed-mix next step covers it.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: Every open caveat says when it would matter and why the trade holds until then. The unnamed behaviour-check judge does not touch the overall-quality judge, which is calibrated on 200 ratings at 86% agreement. Unpaired scoring could only narrow the intervals. Best-of-several could only cheapen Atlas-L. Unknown routing appears in the confidence block, in Watch and in a next step. Each confound has a next step: paired re-run, judge calibration, recording the provider. The routing caveat could sit closer to the cost claims (see findings).

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names a declaration or an experiment and what it would settle. The price per point or floors decide between Atlas-M and Atlas-L and whether the cheaper models stay in. The paired re-run narrows the unsettled band. A routed Atlas-M plus Open-70B mix is offered as an unmeasured option to run, not priced. Judge calibration tests whether the check shortfalls are real. Recording provider, cost coverage and volume makes the bands portable and lets the trade be priced per month.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: The price-frontier, troubleshooting-checks, confirms-gap, speculation-test and atlas-gap-by-task blocks each show their claim's own figure. Four blocks fall short. persona: the claim's cost comparison ($6.40 against $17.00) is not in its block. latency: the claim says 'slowest in every task' but the block draws only research questions. atlas-gap-by-task: the caption says 'overall and in each place', but no overall row is drawn. price-frontier: the caption asserts something about Open-70B that the block does not draw.

findings.finding: The decision block's 'Open-70B is the better buy at no price' and the price-frontier caption's 'Open-70B is never the cheapest way to a point' hold on point estimates only. Open-70B's pooled overall quality is 85.49 ±0.69, against Brisk-S's 84.70 ±0.69. A point bought from Brisk-S to Open-70B costs $6.96 and one from Open-70B to Atlas-M costs $4.58, on gaps whose intervals are about ±1 point. Within those intervals Open-70B could be the best buy for a band of roughly $3.7 to $5.4 a point. Say 'on point estimates Open-70B is never the better buy; within the $4.15 to $6.11 band this run does not separate it from Brisk-S and Atlas-M'. Apply the same wording to the explore row on price per point.

'Brisk-S and Open-70B score lower on all three' reads as a separation, set against 'not told apart' for the Atlas pair. Brisk-S's citing gap to Atlas-M is +5 with an unpaired interval of 0 to +10, which does not clear zero. Open-70B's three gaps and Brisk-S's tool-use and unsupported-claims gaps do clear it. Say that Brisk-S's citing shortfall is not separated.

The lead claim, the headline's '0.42 times' and the persona claim's $6.40 against $17.00 all compare costs. None of them carries the unknown-routing caveat at the claim. The cost_served_by fact says no provider or pricing is stated for any of the four models. The confidence block and Watch disclose it, but the claims that rank models by cost should too. Attach the routing caveat to price-frontier and persona. Add 'on this run's unnamed provider routing' to the headline's cost ratio and the persona cost comparison. This matters most for Open-70B, an open-weights model whose price depends on who hosts it.

The claim's cost comparison, Open-70B at $6.40 against $17.00 for Atlas-M per 1,000 persona conversations, is not in its block, which draws only staying in character. Add the persona cost per model to the block, or move the cost half to a claim whose block shows it. Also consider noting that Open-70B's persona overall quality (90) is not below Atlas-M's (88). That is the evidence behind the routed-mix next step, and the omitted note 'both sit below Atlas-M in most tasks' hides it.

The claim says Atlas-L is 'the slowest model in every task', but the block draws only research questions. Draw p50 to p95 for every task (the appendix has them: Atlas-L's p95 is highest in all five) or limit the sentence to research questions.

The caption says each row is the gap 'overall and in each place both hold it', but the block has no overall row, only the five tasks. Add the pooled overall gap (+2.96, +1.981 to +3.939) as a row, or drop 'overall' from the caption. Also merge the three captions into one.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and lead claim say what is unresolved and why. No price per point was declared, so the owner must choose between Atlas-M and Atlas-L. Below $11.09 a point Atlas-M is the better buy, above $22.05 Atlas-L, and between the two the run does not choose. The main risk is visible: every cost comes from this run's unnamed provider routing, Open-70B's most of all. The headline's 0.42 ratio checks against cost_per_1k ($31.37 against $75.05). The band ends check against price.atlas-m.atlas-l.overall.per_point_low_unpaired and per_point_high_unpaired.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: Each claim matches its block row by row. In atlas-gap-by-task, every task that carries traffic clears zero and speculation bait does not (-1.546 to +3.546). items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: Atlas-M's weak axis, 2.96 points of overall quality behind Atlas-L (+1.981 to +3.939), is stated in full. Research-checks now says Brisk-S's citing gap (0 to +10) is not separated. Two framings still run ahead of their intervals. The persona claim says Open-70B 'scores 90 on overall quality against 88 for Atlas-M', which reads as a lead. items.name: Confounds handled

Unknown routing is now attached to price-frontier and persona and named in the headline. The unpaired intervals have a paired re-run as a next step. items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Last round's fixes landed: the persona block now carries cost and overall quality, and the latency block draws every task. The atlas-gap-by-task caption still promises an overall row, but the next caption line states the pooled gap and says there is no overall row, so a reader is not misled. One block still misses its claim. Confirms-gap states a gap, 17 points (+11 to +23), but its block draws only each model's level. It repeats the troubleshooting-checks column exactly, and the claim's own interval appears nowhere in the block.

findings.finding: The lean says 'Atlas-M, while a point of overall quality is worth less than $11.09 per 1,000 conversations'. Its only reason given is that no behaviour check separates Atlas-M from Atlas-L. But the same decision block and the explore row name Brisk-S the better buy below $4.15 a point. Either bound the lean ('from $6.11 to $11.09 a point'), or say outright that it passes over Brisk-S at low prices because of its behaviour-check shortfalls (resolves 74% against 90%, confirms 88% against 98% in troubleshooting).

'Open-70B scores 90 on overall quality against 88 for Atlas-M' reads as a lead. The unpaired gap is +2 (-0.12 to +4.12, compare.open-70b.atlas-m.overall.task.persona.interval) and does not clear zero. Say Open-70B is not told apart from Atlas-M on persona overall quality, 90 against 88. That is still the evidence the routed-mix next step needs.

The claim states a gap: Open-70B confirms before account changes 17 points less often than Atlas-M (+11 to +23). The block draws only the four levels, which repeat the troubleshooting-checks column, and the claim's interval is nowhere on it. Draw the gap itself, each model less Atlas-M with its unpaired interval, so the +11 to +23 a reader is told is the figure they see.

The unstated-judge caveat covers every behaviour check: confirms, cites, toolcall, unsupported, declines and character among them. Only troubleshooting-checks carries it. Confirms-gap, research-checks, speculation-test and persona (staying in character) all read those checks without it, and the lede's 'fall clearly behind ... confirming before account changes' rests on them. Attach the judge caveat to these four claims. In the lede, soften 'clearly' for Open-70B on resolving, whose gap to Atlas-M is +8 (+0.9 to +15.1).

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Last round's confirms-gap finding is resolved: the block now draws each gap to Atlas-M with the unpaired interval the claim quotes (+11 to +23, +4.9 to +15.1). The other blocks show their claims' own figures. troubleshooting-checks and speculation-test state gaps (+16, +17) over level tables, but the intervals don't overlap, and arms_compare puts the gaps at +8.2 to +23.8 and +10.3 to +23.7, so the levels carry the claims. The template caption 'overall and in each place' on the diverging bars is corrected by the analyst's added line and omitted note. I logged it as a tool gap, not a finding.
